study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities unveil two neuroanatomical obsessive-compulsive disorder subtypes

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression was used to estimate the normative range of regional gray matter volumes from age and sex in healthy controls. The model was trained on HCs and then applied to each patient to generate predicted GMVs, followed by Z-score calculation to quantify deviations.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: we trained a Gaussian process regression model to estimate the normative range of regional GMVs from age and sex in HCs according to the brain connectome atlas
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Wen2025.pdf.md: METHODS / Subtyping analysis based on individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Voxel-wise gray matter volume (GMV) was derived using voxel-based morphometry in the CAT12 toolbox. Regional GMVs were parcellated using the brain connectome atlas (246 regions).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Voxel-wise gray matter volume (GMV) for each participant was derived using voxel-based morphometry in the CAT 12 toolbox

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as predictors in the Gaussian process regression normative model to estimate the expected regional gray matter volumes in healthy controls.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we trained a Gaussian process regression model to estimate the normative range of regional GMVs from age and sex in HCs
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Wen2025.pdf.md: METHODS / Subtyping analysis based on individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities
